rows.en:
I'm Nozomu Kazama.
I'm a third-year.{p}

Honestly, the newspaper club sure has a death wish.
Putting together a feature on this school's seven wonders...
I can only assume you don't know how terrifying spirits really are.
Truth is, I had no intention of agreeing to this interview, but that Hino guy bowed his head and practically begged me.
And on top of that, I heard the one coming to interview us was a new girl.
I could never just ignore a girl being put in danger.
I can tell, you see. Clear as day.{p}

You...
Your name was {b}, wasn't it?
You're about to go through something terrifying, very soon.
Something that will make your hair stand on end...{p}Even so, do you have the courage to hear my story?
Yes, I do
No, I don't

The saddest, most terrifying ghost story in this school...
It's a story deeply tied to a certain place.
A haunted spot?
...Well, something like that.
But I'd rather not use that name.
Why, you ask?
For everyone's sake...
When you hear 'haunted spot,' what kind of place do you all picture?
A graveyard?
An intersection where accidents keep happening?
Or a famous suicide spot?{p}With your impoverished imaginations, that's about as far as you can get, isn't it?
Maybe so...
That's not true at all!
See?{p}

I don't want any of you holding on to fixed ideas like that.
That's why I deliberately avoid the words 'haunted spot.'
Listen, okay?
Spirits are everywhere.
In your classrooms.
In your homes.
In your rooms.
From the drawers of your dresser to the inside of a bucket...
Spirits exist absolutely anywhere.
The place I'm about to tell you about seems to have nothing at all to do with spirits. It's somewhere everyone uses every day without a second thought.
...Let's see.
The easiest way to understand would be to go there.
What kind of place is it...?
That's a surprise for when we get there.
What do you say?{p}Will you come with me?
I don't mind going
I don't want to go

Then let's go right away.
We can't waste any time.{p}

Here we are.
You can tell where we are at a glance, right?
That's right!
The shoe lockers.
...Huh?
What's wrong, {b}?
Standing there with your mouth hanging open like that.
You're spoiling that pretty face of yours.
...Could it be?{p}
Do you doubt my story?{p}You aren't thinking there couldn't possibly be any spirits in a place like this, are you?
Yes, that's what I think
No, I don't think that

Good grief, you still don't seem to understand what I told you.
If you keep thinking like that, something terrible is going to happen to you any minute now.{p}

Look closely. Really strain your eyes.
See, there, that dim spot in the corner of that shoe locker.
Can't you see something around there?
A hazy swirl of lingering will...
A faint white shadow floating in the air...

Hmm...!
Now I'm certain.
The source of that overwhelming aura is deep inside these shoe lockers!
.........Oh, right.
You thought there couldn't possibly be spirits in a place like this, didn't you?
And judging by that face, you still think so.
Then you should check for yourself.{p}

Look, doesn't this shoe locker seem suspicious?
The name and number are fading away, so you can hardly read them, right?{p}Go on, try opening it.
Open it
Don't open it

Oh?
You're not going to open it?
So you're scared after all.
.........That's odd.
You're not answering at all...{p}

Ah, I see!
You're so terrified you're at a loss for words.
{b}, you don't have to hold back.
If you're scared, jump right into my arms.
Come on!

...Oh?
Now you're trembling!
What's wrong?
Are you cold?
Or did something sad happen to you?
Ah, I can almost see it: over your trembling shoulder, the figure of a girl standing there with a sorrowful face.
Come to think of it, there was a rumor about a schoolgirl who killed herself five years ago after getting her heart broken...
Yes, that's it!{p}

It must be her spirit that appears at these shoe lockers.
She was a reserved girl who could never confess to someone she liked.
The type who could manage no more than slipping presents or letters into that person's shoe locker.
...I've got it!{p}

She was in love with whoever used this shoe locker.
Once, somewhere in these shoe lockers, her heartfelt letters and presents were quietly left...
But sadly, her feelings never reached that person.
Unable to bear her grief, the girl killed herself...
Even so, her love didn't fade, and she stays on as a spirit in this place, the only place she ever entrusted her feelings to...
What a sad fate.
{b}, don't you think so?
What was it she poured her feelings into...?
Don't you want to know?
Maybe it's still hidden away somewhere in these shoe lockers, even now.
Waiting for someone to accept her feelings...
That's it!
For her to be freed from the hold these shoe lockers have on her, someone has to throw them open.
Now, {b}.{p}For her sake, open the shoe locker.
Open it
Don't open it

{b}...
What is it you're so worried about?
It isn't the spirit you're afraid of, is it?
Let's see...
If anything, it seems like you're worried about what other people will think.
Am I right?{p}

.........You silly thing.
Sure, it touches on someone's privacy a little.
But it's not like we're going to peek into a safe or a diary.
You're a budding newspaper reporter too, aren't you?
You have my personal guarantee.
This is a legitimate interview.
As part of your seven wonders coverage, you have a duty to investigate these shoe lockers.{p}Now, don't hold back. Open whichever shoe locker you think is the one.
Open it
Don't open it

"Huh, you're no fun.
It's actually pretty interesting, you know.
Look, like this."

With that, Kazama flipped open a nearby shoe locker.
"Oh? Now this is a nice find."{p}

"Huh★
W-Wait, Kazama?"
I got caught up in it and peeked inside too.
But.........{p}

And yet Kazama was getting all excited by himself...
What on earth did he think he'd found?
"Hmm, hmm... Mmm! Hmmm..."
It looked like he was reading something.
Even though there was nothing in his hands...
Was he just making fun of me?{p}

"Hey, how long are we going to stay here?"
Oh no!
The other members were starting to get bored.
So I wasn't the only one who was fed up with Kazama's story.
I couldn't believe things had turned out like this, and on the very first story...{p}What should I do?
Urge Kazama: "Let's head back now."
Leave Kazama behind and go back first

rows.en: Stay with Kazama until he's satisfied

Forget Kazama, I'm going back to the club room.
"Everyone.
It looks like Kazama is doing some important research, so why don't we head back to the club room first so we don't get in his way?"
The others nodded silently.{p}

"Kazama, we're going back to the club room ahead of you."
".................."
...Was he even listening?
"Go right ahead and take all the time you like, until you're satisfied."{p}
Back in the club room, just as we'd caught our breath...

Oh, it sounded like someone was coming.
Could it be the seventh person...?{p}

"Heeey, {b}!"
...Oh, it was just Kazama coming back.
He didn't have to come back until the meeting was over.

"Come on, don't just stand around. Open the door for me."
Honestly!
He could at least do that much himself...{p}"{b}? Aren't you going to open it?"
Open the door
Don't open the door

Fine, fine, I'm opening it now...
"Kazama, you could at least open a door yoursel... Huh★"{p}

Kazama wasn't there.
There was no one outside the door...
While I stood there dumbfounded.........
"What's wrong, {b}?
Don't just stand there forever. Hurry up and get back to your seat."
...That voice?{p}

"Kazama★"
There he was, sitting in his own seat as if nothing had happened.
What on earth was going on?
When had he come into the room?
In that one tiny instant when I opened the door...?
Had everyone else seen him do it?
"{b}?
The host can't be spacing out like that.
Everyone's busy, and they've gone out of their way to make time to be here, you know."
...How selfish could one person be?
Who was the one who wasted everyone's precious time?
I couldn't believe someone this flaky had a sixth sense.
Who knew how much of that story earlier was even true...
Forget it.
Getting too involved with this guy just wore me out.
The best thing to do with someone like this was ignore him.
I sat down in my seat and said, in as calm a voice as I could manage:
"Well then, shall we move on to the next story?"{p}

I see...
So you're a little scaredy-cat.
But it's already too late.
Your terrifying experience began the moment you showed up in this room.
And what's more, you chose me first.
The moment you did that, the door of fate swung open.
I'm going to tell my story.
If I did something as half-hearted as stopping now, it would only stir up the spirits.{p}

Are you scared?
It's all right, I'm here with you.
If you're nervous, I'll hold your hand for you.
You're fine...?
There's no need to be shy about it.
There, now you feel safe, don't you?
Well then, I'll tell my story.{p}

But take a look at the other members' faces.
See how they're all looking down and mumbling?
They're embarrassed that I pointed out the limits of their imagination.
The moment someone says 'haunted spot,' the picture in their heads gets stuck in a rut.{p}

{b}, that just won't do.
I made a big decision to take part in this meeting too, you know.
No matter how much you say you don't want to go, I'll drag you there by force if I have to.
That's right...
I'll carry you there in my arms if I have to.
Would you like that better?
............No?
I see...{p}

It's all right.
You don't have to deny it in such a hurry.
{b}...
You think there aren't any ghosts in a place like this.
I can tell the moment I look at your face.{p}

How sad.
So you don't trust me even the tiniest bit?{p}

"Oh! So you'll open it.
{b}, you've finally made up your mind...
That's right.
For the sake of that poor girl who killed herself, open the shoe locker!"{p}

Just as Kazama told me, I reached out toward one of the shoe lockers.
I don't know why, but I couldn't stop feeling strangely drawn to that one.
What in the world could be inside...★

What? There's nothing in it at all.
And yet Kazama went,{p}

With that thought, I peered in one more time, but the locker was still empty.
Kazama was carefully taking 'something' out of that empty space as if it were precious.
But the shoe locker was empty, I tell you.
There were no shoes, not even indoor shoes.
At least, that's how it looked to me.{p}
Fine, I don't care anymore!{p}

"Everyone, why don't we keep Kazama company just a little longer?
I think this is his own way of helping with our interview.
His strange behavior is an act, so that we don't get too tense.
I'm sure of it..."
It wasn't that I wanted to win everyone over for Kazama's sake.
I just wanted to convince myself that it was true.
But everyone's reaction was cold.
"Then why don't you stay here with him by yourself?
We'll go back to the club room ahead of you."
What?{p}W-wait a minute.
Urge Kazama: "Let's head back now."
Leave Kazama and go back first
returns: 56:3440: RETURN - choice 'Leave Kazama and go back first' vs S209 56:1f78 'Leave Kazama behind and go back first' for near-identical source; editorial may unify.

rows.en: Well, it can't be helped.{p}

I can't go along with Kazama's selfishness anymore.
"You can at least open the door yourself."
"Wha-★
You're telling me to open the door myself?
You've got some nerve, saying something so outrageous to someone like me."
...Honestly!
Just because he's a senior, what does he take me for?
How rude can you get.
I'm definitely not doing it!
"Do you really think it's all right to keep someone like me waiting?{p}Hurry up and open the door."
Open the door
Don't open the door

"You'd better open it."
One of the members muttered it quietly.
"You got here last, so it's only natural you don't know, but...
When he first came here too, he wouldn't come into the room until someone opened the door for him like that."

"{b}, can you hear me?
Hurry up and open the door for me☆"
Kazama was calling again.
As if reacting to his voice and the knocking, the desks began to rattle.{p}

Next, the floor heaved and warped, and pounding on the door and walls rang out.
An earthquake★
No!
It's the sound of knocking.{p}

"Hurry!
Hurry and open the door☆"
I ran to the door, nearly tripping over myself.
Then I flung the door wide open.
And then...?{p}

The shaking that had been so violent stopped dead.
Outside the door, Kazama stood there with a sulky look on his face.
"Honestly, you've got some nerve, keeping someone like me waiting."
With that, Kazama went straight to his seat and sat down.{p}

"You're the host, aren't you?
Would you hurry up and move on to the next story?
I've had enough of being kept waiting."
...How selfish can a person be?
He won't even open a door himself, yet he says whatever he likes.
I can't believe a careless person like this has a sixth sense.
Who knows how much of that story he just told was even true.
...But still.
I have to keep all of this to myself.
When I was closing the door, I saw it.
A huge crack running through the club room door...
Just how strong is he?
Let sleeping dogs lie.
It's best not to get involved with people like him.
I'm sure everyone else thinks so too.
Okay, let's move on to the next story before he gets angry.{p}

"So you'll try opening it.
You've got quite a lot of nerve yourself.
All right, then let's open it.
This shoe locker, right?"{p}

With that, Kazama reached for the shoe locker...
Ah...{p}...Wait a second!
I've changed my mind, never mind
I'll open it myself
I'll pick a different shoe locker

"I've changed my mind!"
I shouted it on the spot.
But it seemed I was a little too late...
Kazama had already flung the shoe locker's door wide open.
Inside it was...★{p}

A nauseating stench stung my nose.
What a horrible smell!
It smelled like a dead crayfish left in a tank for two or three days.
It seemed kind of musty too.
Could this be the source of the aura swirling in the shoe locker?
If so, it was a monstrously vicious aura, full of hatred.
What do I do...
I can't stop shaking.
I've opened something terrible.
That's how it felt.
Kazama was staring into the shoe locker too, as if glaring at it.
And then, slowly, he closed the door...{p}
returns: 56:3f40: RETURN - narration switches between past and present tense mid-paragraph ('What do I do... I can't stop shaking... That's how it felt'); source is present-tense inner monologue, editorial to smooth.

rows.en:
"...Phew, that was a truly awful smell.
Who's the one who never washes their shoes?!
Once it gets that bad, it's a crime."
What★
That was the smell of shoes?{p}

"How truly frightening!
It gives me chills to think someone actually wears shoes like that.
Don't you agree, {b}?"
"............Um, sure."
I mean, that's true, but...{p}

"Well...
Now that we've had a frightening experience, shall we head back to the club room?
Or do you want to try opening another one?"
No way.
I never want to smell anything like that again.{p}

Cursing my bad luck, I hurried to the club room.
Let's see...
Who should I pick next?
Yeah, I'll go with that person.{p}

Back in the club room, once I'd caught my breath, I looked straight into the eyes of the person I'd chosen earlier.
"Now then, the next story, please."{p}

What...
It's just a plain old shoe locker, nothing special about it.
There's only a pair of indoor shoes inside.
...Or so I thought.{p}

Eww!
The soles are crammed with thumbtacks!
Whoever owns these indoor shoes must be really hated.
Or maybe they're being bullied...
I hope it's just someone's prank.
Looking at the rows of thumbtack points, I start to think that the scariest thing of all might be the human heart.
Or else...
Could this be the work of an evil spirit too?
With trembling hands, I closed the shoe locker's door.{p}

"{b}, it looks like you've had a pretty frightening experience.
Your face has gone white as a sheet."
"...Yes."
"Well then, shall we head back to the club room?"{p}

Back in the club room, once I'd caught my breath, I made an effort to keep my voice calm.
"Now then, let's move on to the next story."{p}

Huh, what's this?
What caught my eye was a pink envelope...
Could this be a love letter★
Eeek, what do I do?
..........Oh, it isn't addressed to me.
Geez, all that heart-pounding for nothing.{p}

"Oh? Now this is a nice find."
"Huh★
W-wait a minute, Kazama?"
Don't tell me he's going to read what's inside without asking......

Oh no, he opened it.
Reading someone else's letter without permission...
Isn't that a real crime?

Ah, and on top of that, he's putting the letter he just read in his pocket.
Honestly!
What kind of person is he?
I'm more scared of him...
"Well, shall we hurry back to the club room?
Otherwise it'll throw off the rest of my schedule.
I'm a very busy man, you see."{p}

Honestly, he only ever says whatever suits him!
Kazama's the one who brought us here in the first place!
Everyone else seems a little fed up too.
If today's interview ends in failure, it'll be all, all Kazama's fault.
Really, why on earth did Hino invite someone like this?
Cursing my bad luck, I hurried to the club room.
Let's see...
Who should I pick next?
Yeah, I'll go with that person.{p}

"I'll open it myself!"
I shouted it on the spot.
"Oh?
Then I'll let you do the honors."
Just as Kazama told me, I reached out toward one of the shoe lockers.
I don't know why, but I couldn't stop feeling strangely drawn to that one.
What in the world could be inside...★

"I'll pick a different shoe locker!"
I shouted it on the spot.
"Oh?
Then which shoe locker will it be?
Go ahead and choose for yourself."
Just as Kazama told me, I reached out toward one of the shoe lockers.
I don't know why, but I couldn't stop feeling strangely drawn to that one.
What in the world could be inside...★
